gap: No result ChatGPT got states load power on a common basis: in the same Liliputing 100 GB-copy test (same reviewer, Ian W Morrison), the UGREEN DXP480T Plus drew about 55 W writing to the NAS and the TerraMaster F8 SSD Plus drew 36.2 W with eight drives, and Asustor's '17.9 W (Operation)' rating for the Flashstor 6 Gen2 is about half of the 32.8 W KitGuru measured during writes.
standout_why: I read three rival pages. ComputingForGeeks (cited, updated 2026-10-21) already gives idle watts for all three main picks (FS6806X 13.1 W, F8 SSD Plus 19.7 W, DXP480T Plus about 18 W) and the lanes for each slot. It gives no load watts for these three and no power adapter ratings, and it doesn't point out that the makers' 'operation' figures mean different things. HomelabCompass (cited, 2026-11-02) has no power figures and no lane counts. StarryHope's best-NVMe article (2026-11-02) gives the lanes for each slot, including the FS6806X x4/x2/x2/x2/x1/x1 split and the F8's ASM2806 switch, but no power figures. The idle numbers and the lane footnote are already out there. Only the load-power comparison and the mismatch between maker ratings are new.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The F8 SSD Plus and FS6806X draw roughly the same at load (about 33–42 W). The DXP480T Plus draws about 13 W more when writing a 100 GB file (55 vs 41.6 W at peak in Liliputing's tests) and comes with a 140 W adapter, against 90 W and 72 W for the other two. That is the price of its i5 and its x4 Gen4 slots, and it matters only to buyers who care about power under heavy use. At idle the three are within 6.6 W of each other, which works out to about 58 kWh a year left on 24/7. The page can footnote that maker wattage figures can't be compared: Asustor's 17.9 W 'operation' sits between KitGuru's idle and load readings, and TerraMaster's roughly 45 W is a worst case with all eight drives reading and writing.

findings.label: Maker-stated power
findings.note: The page states no drive count or workload for 'Operation'. Its only test-drive footnote names a Seagate IronWolf 16TB HDD, which this box can't hold, so the footnote looks like it was copied from a hard-drive model's template.

findings.label: Measured power at the wall
findings.value: 13.1 W idle; 27.2 W average reading; 32.8 W average writing
findings.source_title: KitGuru: Asustor Flashstor 6 Gen 2 FS6806X NAS review (Simon Crisp, 2025-02-26)
findings.note: Load was measured during CrystalDiskMark runs, with a drive mix KitGuru doesn't specify. Against the maker's 17.9 W, the write reading is 32.8 / 17.9 = 1.83×, about 83% higher.

findings.label: M.2 interfaces and adapter (maker)
findings.value: 1× PCIe 4.0 x4, 3× PCIe 4.0 x2, 2× PCIe 4.0 x1; 90 W adapter; ECC supported (8 GB DDR5-4800 pre-installed, 64 GB max); 3-year warranty
findings.note: The spec page doesn't say which slot number gets which link width. It lists max capacity as '108 TB (18 TB HDD X 6)', another hard-drive template line, so don't use it as an SSD capacity. Total slot lanes: 4 + 3×2 + 2×1 = 12 Gen4 lanes.

findings.label: Measured power and noise, 8 × 4 TB SSDs
findings.value: 19.7 W idle @ 33.0 dBA; 36.2 W copying 100 GB PC→NAS; 41.6 W copying 100 GB NAS→PC @ 40.3 dBA; 2.2 W powered off
findings.source_title: Liliputing: TerraMaster F8 SSD Plus Review: Up to 64TB of SSD storage (Ian W Morrison, 2024-10-13)
findings.note: Drives elsewhere in the review: 4× Lexar NM790, 2× Samsung 990 Pro and 2× PNY CS2241, all 4 TB. The power section doesn't restate the drive setup.

findings.label: Lane layout and adapter
findings.value: i3-N305 has 9 PCIe Gen3 lanes: 2 to Ethernet, 4 to drives 1–4 (x1 each), 2 to an ASM2806 switch feeding drives 5–8; about 984.62 MB/s per drive; 72 W (12 V 6 A) adapter
findings.source_title: Liliputing: TerraMaster F8 SSD Plus Review: Up to 64TB of SSD storage (Ian W Morrison, 2024-10-13)
findings.note: My arithmetic: 6 Gen3 lanes reach the drives in total, about 5.9 GB/s across all eight slots. Drives 5–8 share the 2-lane uplink, about 1.97 GB/s combined.

findings.label: Measured power, 4 SSDs
findings.value: 14 W idle; 35 W writing to all four drives while saturating the network
findings.source_title: The DIY Life: I Tried The New TerraMaster F8 SSD Plus, Is It Any Good? (Michael Klements, 2024-09-18)
findings.note: Four Crucial P3 Plus drives. Compared with Liliputing's eight-drive 19.7 W, that is about 5.7 W less idle with four fewer drives.

findings.label: General running power and adapter
findings.value: 22–42 W while running; 72 W 12 V brick; 35–36 dBA in a 34 dBA room
findings.source_title: ServeTheHome: TerraMaster F8-SSD Plus Power Consumption and Noise (Patrick Kennedy, 2024-10-02)
findings.note: STH doesn't split idle from load or state the drives used. A reader comment on the page quotes TerraMaster's spec as '45.0 W (Fully loaded Seagate 2TB M.2 SSDs in read/write state)', but I couldn't open TerraMaster's own page to confirm it.

findings.label: Measured power
findings.value: about 18 W idle (UGOS Pro, Ethernet); about 42 W copying 100 GB from NAS; about 55 W copying 100 GB to NAS; about 61 W average / 82 W initial peak under CPU stress; 1.4 W off
findings.source_title: Liliputing: UGREEN NASync DXP480T Plus Review (Ian W Morrison, 2024-09-10)
findings.note: Same reviewer and same 100 GB copy method as the F8 review above, so the load numbers compare like for like. The power section doesn't state the drive count; the review used four Samsung NVMe drives overall. Write load: 55 − 36.2 = 18.8 W more than the F8 SSD Plus. Read load: 42 vs 41.6 W, about equal.

findings.label: Lane layout and adapter
findings.value: Bays 1–2: PCIe Gen4 x4; bays 3–4: PCIe Gen4 x2; separate Gen3 x2 M.2 2242 OS slot; 140 W (20 V 7 A) adapter
findings.source_title: Liliputing: UGREEN NASync DXP480T Plus Review (Ian W Morrison, 2024-09-10)
findings.note: Liliputing says Gen4 for bays 3–4. ComputingForGeeks reports that TechRadar says Gen3, so the generation of the x2 pair is still disputed. Total storage lanes: 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 = 12.

findings.label: Idle power, comparable basis (rival already has it)
findings.value: FS6806X 13.1 W (six SSDs); DXP480T Plus about 18 W (four); F8 SSD Plus 19.7 W (eight)
findings.source_title: ComputingForGeeks: Best All-Flash NVMe NAS (2026): Lanes vs 10GbE
findings.note: I'm listing this so the page doesn't present idle watts as new. 19.7 − 13.1 = 6.6 W × 8,760 h ≈ 58 kWh a year.
